what_this_is: Reads a Pyth price from a guardian-signed attestation, on chain: verifies the VAA, proves the price message is inside the signed Merkle root, and applies the freshness and confidence policy. The number no longer comes from our adapter.
what_changed: WormholeVaaVerifier proved the guardians signed some bytes; the price itself was still a number our adapter pulled out and told you about. A dishonest adapter could pair a genuine attestation with a different price and every signature check would pass. Now the number comes out of the signed Merkle root on chain.
policy_on_chain: Staleness and confidence used to be checked by our adapter — the party who benefits from being trusted. Both are enforced here, so a settlement cannot use a stale or wide-confidence price even if our adapter would have allowed it.
what_this_still_trusts: The Wormhole guardian federation and Pyth's publisher aggregate. And it is all Pyth: nothing cross-checks a second provider, so a Pyth-wide fault is a Misharu-wide fault.
verify_it_yourself: npx tsx scripts/deploy-price-reader.ts   # fetches a fresh attestation and repeats all of this
